business-travel.title: Business travel for growing companies
business-travel.seoTitle: Business Travel for SMEs: When a Travel Manager Pays Off
business-travel.description: A plain-English guide for Australian small and mid-sized businesses: signs you've outgrown booking travel yourself, how travel managers charge, and what to ask.
business-travel.lede: Most businesses start by booking their own flights. At some point that stops being the cheap option. Here's how to tell, what a travel management company actually does, and what to ask before you sign anything.

sections.h: Signs you've outgrown booking it yourself
list: Someone senior spends hours a month booking, changing and chasing receipts.
Nobody can say what the business spent on travel last year without a spreadsheet afternoon.
When a flight is cancelled at night, the traveller is on their own.
You couldn't say quickly where every traveller is if something went wrong.
Different people book different airlines and hotels, so you get no volume benefits.

sections.h: What a travel management company does
p: A travel management company (TMC) books and manages work travel for your team. Most give you a booking tool for simple trips and real people for complex ones, 24/7 help when plans change, reporting on what you spend, and help writing and enforcing a travel policy.
The part businesses value most is usually not the fares. It's knowing where your people are, having one place to fix problems, and getting your time back.

Pricing varies, so get it in writing. Common models are a fee per booking or change (online bookings usually cost less than ones made with a consultant), a monthly or annual management fee, or a mix. Some charge for after-hours help or reporting; some include it.
Ask for the full fee schedule and a worked example based on last year's trips, so you can compare like with like.

sections.h: Questions to ask before you sign
list: What are all of your fees, including changes, after-hours calls and reporting?
Is there a minimum term or a lock-in, and what does it cost to leave?
Who do my travellers call at 2am, and how fast do they answer?
Can we book ourselves online for simple trips?
How do you track travellers if there's an emergency?
What reports do we get, and how often?
Can you load our travel policy into the booking tool?
Can we keep our airline lounge and frequent flyer programmes?

p: A rough idea of last year's travel spend, how many people travel, your common routes, and what isn't working today. That's enough for a useful first conversation, and enough for us to put a shortlist together.

travel-policy-template.description: Make a clear travel policy for your business in five minutes: approvals, flights, hotels, expenses and duty of care. Free, no sign-up, save as PDF or Word.
travel-policy-template.lede: Choose your rules and your policy writes itself. Save it as a PDF, or copy it into Word. Free, no sign-up, and nothing you choose leaves your device.

faq.q: Does a small business need a travel policy?
faq.a: If more than a couple of people travel for work, yes. A one-page policy stops the same questions coming up every trip, keeps spending consistent, and makes it clear how you look after people while they're away.

faq.q: What should a travel policy cover?
faq.a: Who approves trips, how and when to book, which class to fly, what hotels are reasonable, how meals and expenses are paid and claimed, and what travellers do in an emergency. This template covers all of those.

faq.q: What are reasonable amounts for meals and accommodation?
faq.a: Many businesses use the ATO's reasonable travel allowance amounts as a guide. They're updated every year, so link to the current ATO determination rather than copying figures into your policy.

faq.q: Do we need to look after travellers' safety?
faq.a: Employers have work health and safety duties to workers while they travel. At a minimum, know where people are, check Smartraveller advice for international trips, and make sure travellers know who to call.

about.title: About Shortlisted
about.description: Who runs Shortlisted, why it exists, and how it works for Australian small and mid-sized businesses.
paragraphs: Shortlisted helps small and mid-sized Australian businesses choose providers without wading through sales pitches. You tell us what you need; we come back with a short, honest shortlist and the questions worth asking.

We're starting with business travel, because that's what we know best. Shortlisted is run by Simon Farrugia through Independent Media Network Pty Ltd in Melbourne. Simon works in business travel sales, so he knows how travel managers price, what they're good at and where the catches are.
More categories will follow. If you're shopping for something we don't cover yet, tell us anyway: that's how we decide what to add next.

how-we-make-money.title: How we make money
how-we-make-money.description: Shortlisted is free for businesses. Here's exactly how it's paid for, and how we handle providers we're connected to.
paragraphs: Shortlisted is free for businesses. Providers may pay us when we introduce a business that becomes their customer.
Our founder also works in business travel sales for a travel management company. When a provider we suggest is one we work for, are connected to or are paid by, we tell you before you speak to them.
We never sell your details or add you to a mailing list. We only pass your details to a provider after you say yes.
Our free tools, like the travel policy template, run in your browser. What you type into them stays on your device.

privacy-policy.title: Privacy policy
privacy-policy.description: What Shortlisted collects, why, and who sees it.
paragraphs: Shortlisted is run by Independent Media Network Pty Ltd (Melbourne, Australia). This policy explains what we collect and why.

When you ask for a shortlist, we collect the business details you give us: your name, work email, phone (optional), company, team size, rough travel spend and your message. We use them only to reply and prepare your shortlist.
We pass your details to a provider only after you agree to it, and only to the providers you choose. We don't sell or rent your details, and we don't add you to mailing lists.
Our free tools (such as the travel policy template) run entirely in your browser. What you type into them is not sent to us.
We count visits with privacy-friendly analytics (Cloudflare Web Analytics and Google Analytics) to see which pages are useful. These don't tell us who you are.

To see, correct or delete what we hold about you, email hello@shortlisted.com.au. If you're not happy with how we've handled your information, you can contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (oaic.gov.au).
